title: Existing ind-etale splitting theorem for a geometrically w-contractible ring
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings in a common universe, and give $S$ an $R$-algebra structure. Assume $R$ is w-local [def-weil-pbc-w-local], its connected-component space is extremally disconnected, and $R_m$ is strictly henselian for every maximal ideal $m$ [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. If $S$ is ind-etale over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] and faithfully flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], there exists a ring homomorphism $s:S\to R$ such that $s\circ\operatorname{algebraMap}=\mathrm{id}_R$. These three geometric assumptions are exactly the fields of the source class IsWContractibleRing.

proof.text: Choose the closed-point ideal I as the vanishing ideal of the closed points. Its zero locus is the closed-point set by w-locality. For the faithfully flat ind-etale algebra S, replace S by its retained localization along V(IS). The retained-localization properties and algebraicity of the residue fields make this replacement w-local, preserve faithful flatness, and make its closed points precisely the zero locus of the extended I. This is the construction implemented by Ideal.WLocalization in the existing source proof.

An ind-etale map is weakly etale. Every prime of the replacement lies below a maximal ideal whose contraction is maximal. Strict henselianity at that contraction identifies the local rings there; further localization identifies all prime stalks. Apply the w-local stalk-isomorphism retraction theorem and compose with the replacement map. This entire argument is already proved in IsWContractibleRing.exists_retraction, whose axioms were checked to be only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound; no new Lean statement or open proof is introduced.
